rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for a small pest or insect, including a true bug when taxonomic precision is not important.

example.english: There’s a bug in the kitchen—get it out quickly.
example.traditional: 屋企廚房有隻蟲，快啲攞走佢。
example.jyutping: uk1 kei2 cyu4 fong2 jau5 zek3 cung4 faai3 di1 lo2 zau2 keoi5

rows.note: Use this for a fault in a computer program rather than for a physical insect.

example.english: The system has a bug, so it keeps shutting down by itself.
example.traditional: 個系統出現程式錯誤，搞到成日自己熄機。
example.jyutping: go3 hai6 tung2 ceot1 jin6 cing4 sik1 co3 ng6 gaau2 dou3 seng4 jat6 zi6 gei2 sik1 gei1

rows.note: Use this when the illness bug means a virus or the viral cause of an illness.

example.english: I think I’ve caught a bug, so I’m not going to work today.
example.traditional: 我好似中咗病毒，今日唔返工喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hou2 ci5 zung3 zo2 beng6 duk6 gam1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1 laa3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a concealed device used to listen in or intercept communications.

example.english: The police found a bug in the meeting room.
example.traditional: 警方喺會議室搵到一個竊聽器。
example.jyutping: ging2 fong1 hai2 wui6 ji5 sat1 wan2 dou2 jat1 go3 sit3 teng1 hei3
